solution_capability.d_min_source: d_min truncation this call flips at
solution_capability.physics: direct and dual-space phasing works from resolved atoms, and at this resolution they are resolved - this is the normal working range of SHELXT / charge flipping / Superflip.

budget.coverage: tool input serialization, worker startup, preprocessing, initialization, every native iteration, Fourier/peak extraction and result decoding; at most 2s additional worker cleanup; project-lock queue wait excluded

summary.density_measure: integrated density in a 0.7 A sphere around each peak
summary.ranked_by: integrated density (peak acceptance and the symmetry-ghost filter still run in height order, where a satellite is always the weaker peak)

tier_context.reference: median of the peaks left after the anchor and O allowances - the light-atom (carbon) sea
tier_context.rule: a site is assigned the element whose expected density ratio Z/6 its measured ratio reaches; two elements closer than 25% in Z are not separable this way and the lighter label is used with element_uncertain=true

nitrogen_budget.note: disclosure only. The composition allows this much nitrogen per ASU and none of it was assigned: N and C differ by 17 % in Z (N and O by 14 %), which an unrefined solution map cannot resolve. Place N from chemistry - connectivity, H count, planarity, the chem_hint motifs - or after a converged Ueq (element_scan, probe_site), then edit_atoms reassign

element_assignment.reason: density ratio 1.39 vs the light-atom reference (expected 1.33 for O, tier line 1.15); N differ from O by less than 25% in Z - not separable by density on an unrefined map
density ratio 1.34 vs the light-atom reference (expected 1.33 for O, tier line 1.15); N differ from O by less than 25% in Z - not separable by density on an unrefined map

density ratio 1.20 reaches the C/O tier line 1.15, but the composition's O allowance (2 per ASU) is already taken by stronger peaks; this site could be the O and one of those could be this; N cannot be told from C by density (<25% in Z) - labelled C by convention, not identified

density ratio 1.11 vs the light-atom reference is below the C/O tier line 1.15; N cannot be told from C by density (<25% in Z) - labelled C by convention, not identified; within 10% of the C/O line, so O is not excluded either
density ratio 1.00 vs the light-atom reference is below the C/O tier line 1.15; N cannot be told from C by density (<25% in Z) - labelled C by convention, not identified
density ratio 0.87 vs the light-atom reference is below the C/O tier line 1.15; N cannot be told from C by density (<25% in Z) - labelled C by convention, not identified
density ratio 0.27 is below the H/C line 0.41: too little density for a full-weight light atom - a partly occupied site, a disorder component, or map noise

motifs.evidence: C bonded to 2 O at 1.20/1.37 A - one short C=O and one longer C-O(H/R)

chem_hint.read_from: interatomic distances and ring planarity of the sites just placed - no label, file or composition was consulted; a motif that would need a nitrogen appears in its geometry-only form because C/N is not typed at this stage

ueq_hint.why: the sites were just placed with one shared u - the displacement parameters carry no element information until they have been refined
ueq_hint.after_refinement: validate_structure's light_atom_element_check compares each atom's refined Ueq with the median of its bonded neighbours: a C label on a nitrogen site refines LOW (too_light_label), an over-heavy label HIGH (too_heavy_label), and a planar X(O)2 site is read as nitro or carboxylate from the same numbers (nitro_vs_carboxylate_candidates). Run it before delivering anything whose formula depends on these sites

summary.note: no metal in the composition, so no coordination window was used: elements come from the density tier. O is separated from C by the 33 % step in Z; C vs N (17 %) is NOT decided here - every such site is labelled C with element_uncertain=true. Give those sites an identity with edit_atoms once chemistry (connectivity, H count, the chem_hint motifs) or a converged Ueq (element_scan, probe_site, and validate_structure's light_atom_element_check after refinement - see ueq_hint) supports it

adp_suspects.issue: U very large (ghost atom, wrong element too heavy, or disorder)
